clue.text: The death decree of 20?

explanation.surface: A fatal judgement handed down by destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is KISMET, fate; the second definition uses the older sense of the word, a fixed decree of fate or destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatality is a death in an accident or disaster, and in its older sense a fixed destiny laid down by fate.

clue.text: Go in fear and trembling for hungry cattle

indicators.note: something trembling shakes about, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Approaching something in fear and trembling, as a farmer might with a herd of hungry cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trembling' shakes up the letters of GO and FEAR together; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Forage is fodder such as hay or grass, the food provided for hungry cattle and horses.

clue.text: Irving's part in old Lyceum was no laughing matter

definitions.text: Irving's part in old Lyceum was no laughing matter

parts.words: Irving's part in old Lyceum was no laughing matter
parts.note: Henry Irving, the Victorian actor-manager of London's Lyceum Theatre, was famous for serious, sorrowful roles rather than comic ones

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Irving ran the Lyceum Theatre in London in the late 1800s and was celebrated for Shakespeare's darkest roles.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave, sorrowful drama role is the opposite of comic, hence no laughing matter.

clue.text: Frees clutch and suggests we get moving

explanation.surface: A driver releases the clutch pedal and proposes setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read first as 'lets go' (releases a grip) and then as 'let's go', an invitation to depart.
explanation.definitionFit: To release a grip is to stop holding on; the contraction 'let us go' is a call to start off.

clue.text: Experimental lift off? Try the stairs!

parts.note: to try something is to test it
a flight is a set of stairs

explanation.surface: If the lift is out of order on trial, take the stairs instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lift' in the surface is an elevator; in the definition 'lift off' is an aircraft's take-off.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial run of a new aircraft takes off to see how it performs in the air.

clue.text: A digest of revised prices

indicators.note: revised suggests the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A summary of an updated price list.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary, just as a précis is a short abstract of a text.

clue.text: Got up to aim at Jack for a thorny bunch!

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, to get up
in the game of bowls players bowl their wood at the small white ball called the jack

explanation.surface: Getting up to have a go at a man called Jack, over a bunch of prickly flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: In lawn bowls, a popular British game, players roll balls towards a small target ball called the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a wide vase made to hold cut roses, flowers on thorny stems.

clue.text: Some motive and style for walking across the water

parts.note: a cause is a motive or reason for doing something
a way is a manner or style of doing things

explanation.surface: A purpose and a fashion for strolling over water.
explanation.definitionFit: A causeway is a raised road or path built across water or marshland so people can cross on foot.

clue.text: Here toes wiggle to get their covering back into shape

definitions.text: to get their covering back into shape

indicators.note: wiggling moves things about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Toes wiggle inside a shoe as it is stretched back into shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe tree is a foot-shaped insert that stops a shoe, the toes' covering, from losing its form.

clue.text: It could mean a trial for highwaymen

definitions.text: It could mean a trial for highwaymen

parts.words: It could mean a trial for highwaymen
parts.note: read as a court trial of robbers who held up travellers on the highway, it describes a check on how a vehicle performs on the open road

explanation.walkthrough: Highwaymen were mounted robbers on old British roads; the clue imagines them being tested rather than tried in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A test of a car driven on public roads to check its performance.

clue.text: Not much change for an Algarve tourist

definitions.text: Not much change for an Algarve tourist

parts.words: Not much change for an Algarve tourist
parts.note: the Algarve is the southern coast of Portugal, so the clue points to a coin of Portuguese money of the time

explanation.walkthrough: The Algarve is Portugal's holiday coast; before the euro its currency unit was a small-value coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The former Portuguese unit of currency, worth very little, so small change for a visitor.

clue.text: Doing badly on a training crash course

explanation.surface: Struggling on an intensive course of instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'training' is a train ride, and a crash course on one is a derailment; the other sense is the idiom for going wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means going astray or behaving badly; literally it is what a train does when it derails in a crash.

clue.text: Be opposed to anything

explanation.definitionFit: To raise an objection is to disagree; as a noun the word means a thing or item of any kind.

clue.text: Pedigree sleuth?

parts.note: a detective from a pure-bred line, read as a tracking dog of noble breed

explanation.walkthrough: 'sleuth' is a detective but was first a tracking dog; 'pedigree' hints at 'blood' as breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: A large scent-tracking dog used for following trails, a canine detective.

clue.text: A deep down cover-up the divorce judge may have to try!

definitions.text: the divorce judge may have to try

explanation.surface: A judge hearing a divorce suit may have to deal with a scandal kept well hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is feathers stuffing a pillow; the second reading imagines a court case about what was said in bed, pillow talk.
explanation.definitionFit: The fabric cover for a feather-stuffed pillow; read as a lawsuit, a marital dispute that began in bed.

clue.text: Singular direction for one about to make a 4

definitions.text: Singular direction for one about to make a 4

parts.words: Singular direction for one about to make a 4
parts.note: 4 is the trial run of an aircraft, so the one direction a plane takes off in is upwards

explanation.walkthrough: 4-down is TEST FLIGHT; the plane heads up toward the heavens.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards the sky, upwards, the way an aircraft climbs on take-off.

clue.text: A pack game where one tot sounds strangely like another

definitions.text: A pack game where one tot sounds strangely like another

parts.words: A pack game where one tot sounds strangely like another
parts.note: a tot is a small drink of spirit; the card game is named after one spirit, and its second word, a slang term for odd, sounds like a different spirit

explanation.walkthrough: A tot is a measure of spirits: gin is one and the second word, British slang for odd, echoes rum.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-player card game played with a pack, a variant of rummy.

clue.text: Well-endowed crowd barring the multitude without

definitions.text: Well-endowed crowd barring the multitude without

parts.words: Well-endowed crowd barring the multitude without
parts.note: the rich group that excludes the poor masses, those who go without, the have-nots

explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the poor, those who lack; the answer is the phrase 'the have-nots' without its last part.
explanation.definitionFit: The wealthy, those who possess money and property, as opposed to the poor.

clue.text: Sir felt royally touched when he was given one

definitions.text: Sir felt royally touched when he was given one

parts.words: Sir felt royally touched when he was given one
parts.note: a new Sir is tapped on the shoulder with a sword by the monarch, so he is literally touched by royalty

explanation.walkthrough: In a British dubbing ceremony the monarch touches each shoulder with a sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The rank of a knight, which entitles the holder to be called Sir.

clue.text: Being beastly inhuman

explanation.surface: Behaving like an animal, without humanity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word comes from 'brute', an animal, and means savagely cruel and pitiless.

clue.text: The fate of a crowned head meeting troubled times

parts.note: K, for king, a crowned head, as on playing cards and chess notation

indicators.note: troubled times are disturbed, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A monarch's destiny in an age of turmoil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a crowned head' suggests a monarch's literal head, but it is the king's abbreviation from cards and chess; 'troubled' is the anagram signal and 'meeting' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Kismet is destiny or fortune, from the Turkish word for lot or portion.

clue.text: An unloving type whose advances attract excessive interest

definitions.text: An unloving type whose advances attract excessive interest

parts.words: An unloving type whose advances attract excessive interest
parts.note: the advances are loans rather than romantic overtures, and the interest charged on them is extortionate

explanation.walkthrough: 'advances' and 'interest' sound romantic but are financial: loans and the charge on them.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender who charges exorbitant rates on loans.

clue.text: A notability whose value is yet an unknown quantity

parts.note: worth means value
in algebra an unknown quantity is written x, y or z

explanation.surface: An important person whose true value is still a mystery.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthy is an eminent or distinguished person, a local dignitary.

clue.text: See 11
Take-away turnover involving me

annotationWithheld.why: Take-away turnover involving me: REMOVE is ME with an anagram of OVER, but the only indicator is 'turnover', which also supplies OVER, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: A buyer of habits, one might say

definitions.text: A buyer of habits, one might say

parts.words: A buyer of habits, one might say
parts.note: customs are habits, so one who has customs could be called a ..., which is the ordinary word for a shopper

explanation.walkthrough: The word splits as custom plus -er, as if it meant a person of habits.
explanation.definitionFit: A shopper or client who buys goods or services from a business.

clue.text: Pronounces on utter confusion of distress message

parts.note: to utter is to say

indicators.note: confusion jumbles the letters of the call for help

parts.note: SOS is the international distress signal

explanation.surface: Commenting on a muddled call for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion of' turns SOS into SSO; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To declare or state something with authority, as when someone's word settles a matter.

clue.text: I defer acting the false god worshipper

parts.note: to defer acting is to do it later

explanation.surface: I put off performing the role of a false god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'defer acting' is the phrase 'do later', not an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who worships idols, images of false gods.
